main: Global HBM shipment growth in calendar 2027

extras.text: approximately 50%-60%, as the item projects
whether HBM supply remains short of demand in calendar 2027

why: Shipment growth is a supply number, while whether supply still falls short of demand also depends on demand; the article puts both in one sentence, but they can move apart and the shortage drives memory prices on its own.

extras.text: whether any meaningful new HBM capacity comes online before late 2027 (how much new HBM capacity the three main producers bring online)
whether record-high HBM/memory prices persist through late 2027
a supply and input-cost constraint on NVIDIA's GPU shipments

why: The outcome tracks a 'state of HBM supply and pricing' as two equal parts: new capacity arriving and record prices persisting. The capacity part asks 'how much' with no measure, the price part blurs HBM with all memory, and prices can fall from weaker demand even with no new capacity, so no single main thing can be told.

the block that currently keeps NVIDIA's China share at zero despite U.S. clearance
